## Context
`test_dc_corpus_has_eligible_units_that_actually_change` invokes Pandoc for 232 eligible prose units but its only contract is existential: at least one eligible unit exists and at least one changes. Current local runtime is 7.887s/232 subprocesses; an exact short-circuit reaches both witnesses in 0.035s/1 subprocess. Forced identity-renderer and no-eligible mutations fail under both forms. This is exact existential evaluation, not corpus sampling, and matches `any(...)` practice in pytest, Django, and CPython. No tracker rejection was found.

## Plan
- Freeze the existing two existential postconditions and inventory the full-corpus property tests that independently retain corpus-wide conversion coverage.
- Strengthen the existing test oracle to prove iteration stops after both witnesses exist while still failing when no eligible or no changed unit exists.
- Implement exact short-circuit evaluation without changing `_render_unit` or product behavior.
- Run held-out RED→GREEN, defect-seeded mutation, focused corpus tests, repository gates, and paired timing. Back-out is a Gerrit revert.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The test still fails if the stratum has no eligible units.
- [x] The test still fails if every eligible unit renders identically.
- [x] The test stops rendering immediately once both existential witnesses have been observed.
- [x] Full-corpus idempotence, no-decay, richness, and hardening coverage remain unchanged in their existing tests.
- [x] A defect-seeded non-short-circuit mutation returns the held-out oracle to RED.
- [x] Paired timing quantifies saved subprocesses and runner time.
- [x] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, Gerrit LLM-Review +1, and Gerrit Verified +1 pass before merge.
- [x] The final ticket comment records RED/GREEN/mutation evidence and measured savings.
